debit_pay_findings.cards: personal/business Citi cards (Double Cash, Costco Visa, etc.)

Citi stopped taking cash payments at branches years ago (2018), pushing branch/register-style payoffs toward third-party walk-in networks like CheckFreePay instead of Citi's own counters

debit_pay_findings.evidence: Discover's own card-smarts page lists debit card as a standard online payment option alongside ACH; Capital One's Discover migration notes say earning rates and account mechanics are not changing at this stage

debit_pay_findings.limit_note: issuer may cap debit-card payment amount; cannot fund a Synchrony payment with another credit card
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Synchrony's own site and cardholder-support guides confirm debit card is accepted online and via the automated phone line; credit-card-funds-credit-card is explicitly blocked

debit_pay_findings.limit_note: in-person at a Wells Fargo branch only, not online or by phone
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Consumer payment guide (last updated 9/10/26) confirms debit card works only if you physically go into a Wells Fargo branch; online and phone payment options are ACH/checking-savings only

debit_pay_findings.limit_note: no direct debit-card payment on any channel; the closest workaround is inserting the debit card's linked checking account for an ACH-style branch/ATM payment
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Consumer guidance confirms Chase does not accept a debit card directly for online, phone, or branch bill payment; only the linked bank account can be used

debit_pay_findings.limit_note: no direct online/phone/branch debit acceptance; workaround is ATM cash withdrawal on the debit card, then a cash payment in branch or at a U.S. Bank ATM
debit_pay_findings.evidence: U.S. Bank does not accept debit cards for bill pay on any channel per current cardholder guidance; U.S. Bank has separately been described by the MS community as vigilant against gift-card-driven spend abuse (Altitude Reserve shutdowns)

debit_pay_findings.limit_note: Amex explicitly states credit/debit cards are not accepted as a payment form on any channel; cash-advance fee if using one to get cash first is 5% (min $10)
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Amex's own FAQ says credit and debit cards cannot be used to pay an Amex bill; only bank-account ACH, check, or in some cases another bank's bill-pay service works

debit_pay_findings.channel: none (was briefly shown to some accounts online in 2016)
debit_pay_findings.limit_note: current guidance: ACH from checking/savings only, free; late fee $25-$40 if missed
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Doctor of Credit reported in Aug 2016 that Capital One began surfacing a debit-card payment option online for some accounts after long being available by phone ("not available on all accounts currently"); current 2026 consumer guidance says Capital One does not accept debit-card payment on any channel, suggesting the option was rolled back or never fully launched

debit_pay_findings.limit_note: debit card not accepted online, by phone, or in person; ACH from bank account only
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Consumer guidance confirms Barclays does not accept a debit card as a bill-payment method on any channel

debit_pay_findings.cards: "nearly all MasterCard and Visa card bill payments, regardless of issuing bank" per CheckFreePay's own marketing, i.e. can pay most bank-issued credit cards this way even when the issuer's own channels refuse debit
debit_pay_findings.limit_note: fee varies by agent location (not published); cash or debit card accepted at the counter; find locations via their payment-center locator
debit_pay_findings.evidence: CheckFreePay is a Fiserv-owned walk-in bill-payment network embedded in grocery/convenience stores; it is the mechanism behind most "pay your credit card at the register" reports and explicitly separates itself from Plastiq/credit-funded rails by only taking cash or debit at the counter

debit_pay_findings.cards: most major credit card billers listed in MoneyGram's Walmart directory
debit_pay_findings.limit_note: in-store: bring account number, cash or debit card, and biller name; online bill pay via moneygram.com also accepts credit/debit but issuer may code it as a cash advance
debit_pay_findings.evidence: MoneyGram's Walmart bill-pay page confirms cash or debit card at the counter; frequentmiler/pointchaser both separately warn that credit card companies have been known to shut down accounts that receive frequent payments through in-store bill-pay services, and that Walmart specifically clamped down on gift-card-funded money-order/debit MS starting 12/19/2020 (4-swipe cap per visit)

debit_pay_findings.limit_note: payable at any Sam's Club or Walmart register (not the membership desk); Direct Credit accounts must be paid by mail instead; open-to-buy updates immediately for cash/debit
debit_pay_findings.evidence: Sam's Club help-center article confirms register payment with cash or debit restores available credit instantly, a store-register mechanic directly analogous to the Costco MCC-5300 register flow this project cares about

debit_pay_findings.issuer: Melio (business bill-pay app, sometimes cited as a Plastiq alternative)
debit_pay_findings.cards: business bills only; explicitly excludes paying off credit-card/loan debt with an Amex or Visa card
debit_pay_findings.limit_note: ACH and debit-card payments are fee-free through Melio, but Melio bars using it to pay "debt obligations" (credit cards, mortgages, loans) with Amex or Visa specifically; it is built for paying non-card-accepting vendors, not for debit-pays-credit-card MS
debit_pay_findings.evidence: MilesTalk's write-up frames Melio as the fee-free debit-payment alternative to Plastiq for business expenses, but flags it cannot be used to pay down a credit card or loan balance with Amex/Visa - relevant to rule out as a Taekus-style stacking rail

stopped_accepting.scope: single poster reported the phone-IVR debit-payment menu option disappeared entirely for their Costco Visa (call routes straight to bank-account options); last successful debit payment they made was on a 4/15 - unconfirmed by a second source, flagged low-confidence

Doctor of Credit reported Capital One surfacing a debit-card payment option online for a subset of accounts in August 2016 (after it "long been possible" by phone); current 2026 consumer guidance across multiple sources says Capital One accepts no debit-card payment channel at all, implying the 2016 rollout was reverted or never went account-wide

stopped_accepting.scope: Walmart instructed store employees to refuse manufactured-spending-pattern transactions; most stores capped money-order buyers to 4 debit-card swipes per visit (e.g., $2,000 using $500 debit gift cards) - relevant background for anyone routing a Costco-gold debit payoff through Walmart's bill-pay counter

new_card_leads.card: Taekus rewards debit card + checking account
new_card_leads.issuer: Taekus (bank partners: DR Bank / First Federal Bank of Kansas City)
new_card_leads.why_interesting: Invite-only debit card the MS community can't fully decode - one myFICO poster's own tracking showed ~0% back on an Amazon reload, small misc-purchase back, ~2% on a hotel purchase, suggesting merchant-category-dependent rewards rather than a flat rate; no public confirmation either way on bill-payment earning

Discover already takes debit card payments online and Capital One has said earning rates/benefits aren't changing "at this stage" through the 7/27/2026 app migration - worth re-checking after migration completes in case debit-pay is dropped during the platform swap

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: keeping monthly spend on a single card roughly at or below stated annual income divided by 12, since spending far above declared income is a top shutdown/financial-review trigger
ms_criteria.why: issuers read outsized spend-to-income as default or fraud risk, not just reward-chasing

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: Chase and Amex are treated as high-risk/high-scrutiny (Chase can kill an entire banking relationship - cards, checking, UR points - with no warning or appeal; Amex runs formal "financial reviews"); Bank of America, Capital One, and Discover are viewed as more tolerant because their rewards portfolios are smaller and draw less scrutiny
ms_criteria.why: smaller/less rewards-heavy issuers have less to lose per customer and historically enforce less aggressively

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: frequent payments arriving via in-store bill-pay services (Walmart, CheckFreePay-type counters) or via many different debit cards in a short window is called out as a specific shutdown trigger, separate from spend amount
ms_criteria.why: the payment channel itself is a fingerprint of gift-card/MS activity that issuers' fraud/AML models watch for

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: community rule-of-thumb keeps weekly money-order-style cash-equivalent deposits under $3,000 and explicitly avoids repeated just-under-$10,000 patterns, calling deliberate under-threshold structuring illegal
ms_criteria.why: deposits at/near $10,000 trigger a bank's Currency Transaction Report; a pattern of avoidance is itself a Suspicious Activity Report flag under BSA rules

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: community treats issuer-published caps (e.g., an Amex ~$50k/year reference point on a bonused category) as the de facto ceiling to stay under, and is wary of hitting an annual cap suspiciously early in the year
ms_criteria.why: caps mark the point at which the issuer's own economics flip negative, making the account a review target

ms_criteria.what_they_look_for: paying a card off many times per month is flagged as its own red flag independent of total dollar volume, because it doesn't match ordinary consumer payment cadence
ms_criteria.why: payment-frequency anomalies are an easy automated-detection signal even when per-transaction amounts look normal

gold_costco_notes.note: Community frames 1oz Costco PAMP gold bars as a favorite MS vehicle because a single purchase covers a large chunk of a card's minimum-spend requirement while stacking card rewards with Costco Executive membership's 2% annual reward on qualifying purchases

Costco warehouse (in-store) gold purchases require a Visa card; Costco.com online purchases accept both Visa and Mastercard - relevant to which cards can even touch the MCC 5300 spend in the first place

The strategy explicitly assumes paying the card in full every cycle with cash on hand ('don't carry credit card debt to do this') because the gold price spread and resale-platform (e.g., Pure) fees already erode the margin before interest would

No blog or forum surfaced in this sweep discusses Costco gold's specific MCC coding (5300 warehouse club) or issuer shutdown patterns tied specifically to bullion purchases - the bullion-specific shutdown-risk literature (vs general MS risk vocabulary) appears to be a gap in the public MS blogosphere as of this sweep

taekus_notes.note: Taekus is described repeatedly as a 'shadowy, invite-only institution' even by the MS/credit community itself; myFICO thread found no reliable public breakdown of the rewards formula

One user's own tracked cash-back samples on the Taekus debit card: ~0% back on an Amazon gift-card reload, 'very little' on misc purchases, ~2% on a hotel purchase - implying merchant-category-weighted rewards, not a flat rate

Taekus's own CFPB-filed debit card agreement confirms a 'rewards balance' exists as a contractual concept but a forum poster noted it does not describe how the rewards are actually earned - no public source in this sweep confirms or denies whether paying a credit card bill counts as a rewards-earning transaction, or whether there is a monthly cap

Taekus's public site (taekus.com) discloses only that it is 'premium banking services' operating through bank partners DR Bank and First Federal Bank of Kansas City; no rate sheet, cap, or bill-pay terms are published for non-members
